about: Targets for `nvh launch <tool>`. Templates substitute only {base} (the nvHive API base URL, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1) and {key} (HIVE_API_KEY when set, else the documented placeholder nvhive). kind env: the variables reach the tool through its child environment only; kind snippet: the text is printed for the user to paste, nvHive writes no third-party config file; kind mcp: nvHive's MCP server is registered with the tool, which is then launched with inference unchanged. verified_on is null until a maintainer records a run against the tool's current release; every null prints as unverified.

targets.name: claude
targets.snippet:
# nvh launch claude
#   1. claude mcp add nvhive -- nvhive-mcp    (registers nvHive's MCP server; repeatable)
#   2. claude <extra args>                     (inference stays with Anthropic)
# No inference variables are set: nvHive's Anthropic proxy does not pass tool_use
# through, so pointing Claude Code's inference at it would break its tools.
# `nvh launch claude --inference-proxy` prints that snippet anyway, marked unverified.
targets.inference_proxy:
# Claude Code inference through nvHive's Anthropic proxy.
# nvHive's Anthropic proxy does not pass tool_use through, so Claude Code's
# tools would stop working; `nvh launch claude` keeps inference at Anthropic
# and registers nvHive as an MCP server instead.
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL={base}/anthropic
ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN={key}
notes: Registers nvHive as an MCP server (the same `claude mcp add nvhive -- nvhive-mcp` that `nvh integrate` runs) and launches `claude`; inference stays with Anthropic.
nvHive's Anthropic-compatible proxy drops tool_use, which Claude Code needs, so no ANTHROPIC_* variable is set; --inference-proxy prints that snippet marked unverified.

targets.name: codex
targets.snippet:
# ~/.codex/config.toml — nvHive as a Codex model provider
# Codex's default provider speaks the Responses API, which nvHive does not
# serve; wire_api = "chat" keeps Codex on /chat/completions.
model_provider = "nvhive"
model = "auto"

[model_providers.nvhive]
name = "nvHive"
base_url = "{base}"
env_key = "HIVE_API_KEY"
wire_api = "chat"

# Then, in the shell that starts codex (any non-empty value in open mode):
# export HIVE_API_KEY={key}
notes: Codex's default provider speaks the Responses API, which nvHive does not serve: the stanza sets wire_api = "chat" so Codex uses /chat/completions.
env_key names the variable Codex reads the key from; nvHive never writes ~/.codex/config.toml for you.

targets.name: opencode
notes: An OpenAI-compatible provider entry keyed baseURL; the model ids are nvHive routing modes (auto, safe, council).
Paste it into opencode.json yourself; nvHive writes no third-party config file.

targets.name: continue
targets.snippet:
# ~/.continue/config.yaml — nvHive as an OpenAI-compatible model
models:
  - name: nvHive (auto)
    provider: openai
    model: auto
    apiBase: {base}
    apiKey: {key}
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]
notes: The openai provider with apiBase pointed at nvHive; model is a routing mode (auto, safe, council).
Paste it into config.yaml yourself; nvHive writes no third-party config file.

targets.name: cursor
notes: Cursor has no config file for this: the base URL and key are typed into Settings → Models.
A tool that validates its provider against GET /models should use the /v1/proxy base URL instead (GET /v1/models keeps the nvHive envelope).
